oz51x-dual-tx-housing-vertical-gpt-5-6-s.hole_pattern_summary:
CONFIRMED: this housing has NO external mounting ears, flanges, feet, bosses or tabs anywhere. The STEP bbox (32.72 x 133.5 x 92.2) equals the stated finished envelope exactly; nothing protrudes. Two solids: solid0 = tray body x[-16.36,13.36] (97658 mm3), solid1 = removable +X service cover x[9.16,16.36] (36647 mm3). All walls are 3.0 mm (interior faces at x=-13.36, x=13.36, y=-33.25, y=94.25, z=3.0, z=89.2).

The ONLY fastener-capable holes in the entire part are the 6 LID SCREWS, all axis +X, entering the removable cover at x=16.36. Pattern (y, z): (-29.25, 46.1), (0.0, 46.1), (29.25, 46.1), (53.25, 46.1), (90.25, 7.0), (90.25, 85.2). Four of them sit on the horizontal centreline z=46.1 (the inter-bay rib, which spans z 44.1..48.1) and two at the rear plenum y=90.25. Each is: 6.6 dia chamfer mouth at x=16.36 -> 6.0 dia counterbore x[14.76,16.06] (head seat plane x=14.76) -> 3.4 dia clearance x[13.36,14.76] -> 2.5 dia BLIND pilot in a 6.0 dia post running x[12.76,-13.36], i.e. 26.72 mm of pilot ending exactly on the inner floor face with 3.0 mm of floor left. No thread is cut in the STEP; these are self-tapping M3 pilots (housing.corner_post_pilot_dia = 2.5, lid_screw_clear_dia = 3.4, lid_screw_head_dia = 6.0).

The three Z-axis dia-3.0 cylinders are DRAINS, not mounting features (model.py "Gravity-aware drainage for the vertical mounting attitude", refine.drain_dia = 3.0):
 * 2x downward outlets through the -Z bottom wall, z from 0.0 to 3.0, at (x=-11.61, y=20.0) and (x=-11.61, y=44.25). These are OPEN into the lower module bay and into the fiber plenum respectively. They must stay clear.
 * 1x internal cross-drain through the 4.0 mm inter-bay rib at (x=-11.61, y=20.0), z from 44.1 to 48.1, linking upper bay to lower bay. Fully internal, not on any exterior face.

Other holes exist but are all connector fixings, already occupied: 4x dia 1.7 SC/APC flange pilots on +Y and 2x dia 3.2 DE-9 jackscrew holes on +Y.

WHICH FACE IS AVAILABLE TO MOUNT ON: -X (x=-16.36). It is a single planar face, 12305.3 mm2, with ZERO inner wires (zero holes, zero bosses) - a plain 133.5 x 92.2 rectangle with 2.0 mm corner radii. It is entirely part of solid0 (the tray), so no tray/cover joint crosses it. It is the canonical tray floor turned onto its side. Its only defect as a mount face is that it has NO fixings at all. Second choice on flatness is +Z (top, z=92.2): also zero openings, 4237.2 mm2, but split at x=13.36 between the tray (3848.7 mm2) and the removable cover (388.5 mm2). -Z (bottom) is 4223.1 mm2, also split at x=13.36, and carries the two drain outlets.

LID SCREWS AS BRACKET RETENTION: yes, mechanically there is room. Each pilot is 26.72 mm deep and only ~1.4 mm of cover plus a few mm of engagement is consumed today, so the same M3 screws could be lengthened to pick up a plate on +X up to roughly 15 mm thick and still leave >10 mm engagement (max total penetration 28.12 mm below the head seat before bottoming on the floor; 31.12 mm before piercing the -X exterior). BUT the plate would have to be relieved for the 6 vent slots and the 2 header service openings, and removing the cover for service would release the bracket - the load path would run through a 3.0 mm printed cover into 6.0 mm printed posts.

forbidden_mount_faces.why: Carries both SC/APC fiber adapters and the DE-9. The adapter flanges span x[-15.72,6.28] (within 0.64 mm of the -X plane) at z 12.2-24.0 and 68.2-80.0, and the DE-9 flange spans the middle band z 39.5-52.7 across nearly the full width. Between them there is no usable flat land, and 45 mm of straight-out clearance is required for the mated SC/APC plus the 15 mm fiber bend radius.

Carries both SMA bulkhead ports on the axis x=-8.33 at z=10.85 and z=55.95, with mating plugs and coax needing straight-out clearance. Bearing a plate here would also load the 3.0 mm front wall directly over the SMA relief pockets.

This is the REMOVABLE SERVICE COVER (solid1). Three reasons: (1) removing it for module service would release the bracket, so the unit is no longer captive; (2) it carries 6 through vent slots and 2 header service openings that a plate would blank; (3) the load path would run through a 3.0 mm printed cover plate into 6.0 mm printed posts rather than into the tray body.

This is the gravity-DOWN face the drainage was designed around, and it carries both dia 3.0 drain outlets at (x=-11.61, y=20.0) and (x=-11.61, y=44.25). It is also split at x=13.36 by the tray/cover joint, so a plate here would clamp the removable cover.

Not geometrically obstructed (zero openings, 4237.2 mm2) but weak as a mount face: it is split at x=13.36 by the tray/cover joint so a plate straddles and traps the removable service cover, it is only a 3.0 mm wall (interior at z=89.2), and it has no fixings at all.

preferred_mount_face.why: The only face that is large, perfectly flat, completely feature-free and entirely on the tray body. Measured as a SINGLE planar face at x=-16.36 with ZERO inner wires: a 133.5 x 92.2 rectangle with 2.0 mm corner radii, area 12305.3 mm2 - 100 percent of it flat and unobstructed. It is 2.9x the bearing area of the next-best face (+Z, 4237.2 mm2) and, unlike +Z and -Z, no tray/cover joint crosses it, so a bracket there never interferes with removing the +X service cover. Backed by a 3.0 mm floor (interior face x=-13.36) with the 6.0 mm dia screw posts and the bay/plenum ribs immediately behind it. THE CATCH: it has no fixings whatsoever - the part offers no threaded or clearance feature on this face - so attachment must be by clamping, strapping or bonding unless new holes are added. Two measured facts relevant to that: (a) all six 2.5 mm post pilots terminate exactly at the inner floor face x=-13.36, leaving only 3.0 mm of floor between each pilot bottom and this exterior surface, at (y,z) = (-29.25,46.1), (0,46.1), (29.25,46.1), (53.25,46.1), (90.25,7.0), (90.25,85.2); (b) the SC/APC adapter flanges on +Y reach x=-15.72, so any bracket wrapping the -X/+Y corner will collide with them.

unknowns: SMA mating-plug clearance: no SMA connector clearance figure exists anywhere in params.json. The 30.0 mm clear_out on the two -Y SMA keep-outs is my estimate (typical SMA plug body plus coax bend), NOT a sourced number. Confirm against the actual cable assembly before cutting a plate.

DE-9 external mating clearance: params.json only gives panel_connector.rear_keepout_depth = 16.0, which is the INTERNAL solder-cup / wire-bend volume inside the plenum. There is no external figure for a hooded plug plus cable bend. The 40.0 mm clear_out on the +Y DE-9 keep-out is my estimate.

SC/APC adapter flange footprint (22.0 x 11.8 x 3.0, flange_len/flange_wide/flange_thickness in params) is NOT modelled in this STEP - the STEP contains only the cutout and the dia 1.7 pilots. Whether the flange is recessed is not represented; I assumed it stands ~3.0 mm proud of y=97.25. Verify against the physical adapter.

No threads are cut anywhere in the STEP. The six 2.5 mm post bores are self-tapping pilots (housing.corner_post_pilot_dia = 2.5) for M3. Actual thread form, required engagement length and pull-out strength in printed PETG/ABS are not determinable from geometry - the 28.12 mm figure is available pilot depth, not rated engagement.

Cover-removal clearance in +X (how much straight-out space is needed to withdraw the 4.2 mm registration lip plus screwdriver access) is not modelled. I used 60.0 mm for the lid-screw keep-out as a working figure.

DISCREPANCY vs the brief: the -Y SMA holes were stated as z=7.3 and z=52.5. Measured centres are z=10.85 and z=55.95 (dia 7.7 counterbore 0.6 deep into a dia 7.0 through hole, axis x=-8.33). Reconcile which is authoritative before a plate is cut - I am reporting the geometry as imported.

Whether the two -Z drain outlets are intended to remain open in the final installed attitude is a design-intent question, not a geometry one. They are currently open straight into the lower module bay and the fiber plenum.

preferred_mount_face.why: The only face that is flat, unobstructed and has fixings. It is a single continuous plane at y=7.239 covering 22987.7 mm2 with nothing on the part protruding below it (model ymin = 7.239). It carries the only usable fastener features on the whole unit: 4x dia-4.500 through-clearance holes on a 161.800 (X) x 82.700 (Z) rectangle. AVAILABLE FULL-CONTACT AREA BETWEEN THE 4 HOLES: the hole-centre rectangle is 161.800 x 82.700 = 13380.86 mm2; the only interruption inside it is the 0.200 mm deep 65.000 x 40.000 label/foot recess (X -17.362..47.638, Z -60.970..-20.970) which lies entirely inside that rectangle, so true metal-to-metal contact = 13380.86 - 2600.00 = 10780.86 mm2. The recess is not an obstruction, it is 0.200 mm below the bearing plane, so a bracket bridges it freely. Largest single UNBROKEN contact rectangle inside the hole pattern = 48.400 x 82.700 = 4002.68 mm2 (either the strip at X 47.638..96.038 or X -65.762..-17.362); the two transverse strips are 161.800 x 21.350 = 3454.43 mm2 each. Outside the hole pattern there is a further ~9.6 mm of flange all round plus the two 147.000 x 2.000 end tabs. Screw access on the far side of all 4 holes is completely open - verified zero geometry outboard of x=-59.95/90.20 above y=9.80 - so grip is 2.500 mm and screw length past the flange is unconstrained by the unit.

TAPPED-vs-CLEARANCE VERDICT: tapped M3x0.5, high confidence - see unknowns for the exact evidence chain and the one residual risk. Secondary pattern: 4+4 dia-3.200 case-screw clearance holes at X=4.895/112.105, Y=4.000/27.210 on the +Z and -Z panels, feeding M3-tapped PEM AETKS-M3-2 corner standoffs (10.964 mm total depth from the outer face, thread starting 5.436 mm in) - but both those faces are connector faces and the screws retain the panels, so they are not mounting provisions.
unknowns: TAPPED VERDICT AND ITS EVIDENCE. The four -Y bores are M3x0.5 TAPPED, not clearance. Evidence, all from this STEP: (1) the vendor's own BOM name for the insert is PEM_AETKS... no - it is 'SOS_M3-10', i.e. PEM self-clinching standoff, thread code M3, length 10 mm; PEM designates UNTHREADED thru-hole standoffs by hole-size code (SOA-x.x-x), never by an 'M3' code. (2) The bore is modelled at exactly 3.000 mm = M3 nominal/major. The same file uses 3.200 mm for every genuine M3 clearance hole in it - the PCB holes, both panels' case-screw holes, and the upper 4.000 mm of this very standoff - so 3.000 is demonstrably not this author's clearance size. (3) An M3x8 button-head screw with a 3.000 mm shank is modelled engaged in that same 3.000 mm bore; a 3.000 bore cannot retain a 3.000 screw unless it is tapped. (4) The bore is open through the standoff's end face at Y=-1.210, i.e. reachable from outside.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: the STEP contains no thread helix and no AP242 semantic PMI, so 'tapped' is an inference from part identity plus diameter convention, not from modelled thread form. Note also that this file's OTHER tapped feature (PEM AETKS-M3-2 in the panel corners) is modelled at 2.459 mm = exact M3x0.5 MINOR diameter, a different convention from the 3.000 used here - the two PEM models simply came from different sources.

RESIDUAL RISK - PEM catalogues type 'SOS' as a BLIND-threaded standoff (closed at one end). This model shows the bore open clean through to the outer face at Y=-1.210. If the production part is genuinely blind-closed at the clinch end, all four bottom bores would be inaccessible from outside and the whole -Y mounting scheme collapses. VERIFY ON HARDWARE before cutting a plate: run an M3 screw into one bore from underneath, and confirm engagement depth with a depth gauge. This is the single check that would move confidence from high to certain.

Tapped length: the dia-3.000 section runs 6.000 mm (Y=-1.210 to +4.790). Whether the real tap runs that full 6.000 mm from the outer end, or only part of it, is not determinable from the geometry. Use 3.5 mm design penetration regardless, since the PCB screw tip at Y=+2.364 is the hard stop.

Clamp load / torque rating of a clinched PEM SOS in 1.210 mm sheet is not determinable from geometry. If this is a vibration/shock mount, get the PEM pushout and torque-out figures for SOS-M3 in 1.2 mm material.
